name: zim
author: NucleoOS (zim, nvzim, nvhtml); Meta Platforms (zstd); the XZ Embedded authors
description: The offline library in the Terminal: reads Kiwix's ZIM files (Wikipedia, Wiktionary, medicine, iFixit, DevDocs...) copied to ~/zim. Type zim ls, zim search WORDS, zim get TITLE.

descriptions.en: The offline library in the Terminal: reads Kiwix's ZIM files (Wikipedia, Wiktionary, medicine, iFixit, DevDocs...) copied to ~/zim. Type zim ls, zim search WORDS, zim get TITLE.
descriptions.it: La biblioteca offline nel Terminale: legge i file ZIM di Kiwix (Wikipedia, Wikizionario, medicina, iFixit, DevDocs...) copiati in ~/zim. Scrivi zim ls, zim search PAROLE, zim get TITOLO.

usage: zim ls (collections in ~/zim) | zim search [-z NAME] [-n N] TEXT (titles starting with TEXT, any case) | zim get [-z NAME] TITLE [--intro | --section NAME | --sections | --html | --out FILE] [--max N] [--all] (an article as text: --intro = the lead, then the list of its sections; --max caps the whole output in bytes; --all keeps notes and links) | zim TITLE = zim get TITLE | zim random [-z NAME] | zim info NAME | zim check NAME (MD5). NAME = a collection's name, its file name or a unique part of them (medicine). A title is matched exactly first (any case), else the nearest title, else titles and paths containing the words (collections up to 200000 entries). Example: zim get -z wikipedia 'Giuseppe Garibaldi' --intro --max 1500

does.en: Offline encyclopedias, dictionaries, manuals (ZIM files in ~/zim). zim ls lists them; zim search 'words'; zim get 'Title' --intro --max 2000 prints an article as text; -z NAME picks a collection.
does.it: Enciclopedie, dizionari, manuali offline (file ZIM in ~/zim). zim ls le elenca; zim search 'parole'; zim get 'Titolo' --intro --max 2000 stampa una voce come testo; -z NOME sceglie la raccolta.
